o: AWS sizes the launch environment from a submitted traffic forecast and pre-allocates it before the event
A fixed block of launch capacity must be reserved up front and is billed whether or not it is used
Hardware requests are fulfilled from AWS inventory after a lead time of several days
Capacity can be provisioned to match live demand and adjusted afterward
fixes.e: The core change is that you stop guessing capacity: resources are provisioned to match observed demand and resized in minutes as it shifts. AWS does not pre-allocate an environment from a submitted forecast on the customer's behalf, provisioning has no multi-day lead time, and reserving a fixed pre-paid block is an optional pricing choice rather than a requirement for launch capacity.

o: Take nightly snapshots of each instance for later restoration
Spread instances across multiple Availability Zones
Replace instances that fail health checks automatically
Move each instance to a larger size before major on-sale events
Cache the site's static assets on a content delivery network
fixes.e: Spreading instances across multiple Availability Zones survives the loss of a facility, and automatic replacement of unhealthy instances survives the loss of a server. Nightly snapshots only help restore data after an outage rather than keeping orders flowing through one, and larger instance sizes or CDN caching of static assets improve performance without removing any single point of failure.

o: AWS WAF evaluates outbound responses only, leaving inbound requests unfiltered
AWS Shield Standard requires a separate subscription before protection begins
AWS Shield defends against volumetric network layer attacks
AWS WAF rate-based rules can throttle requests from a single source
AWS Shield protects only traffic that first matches an AWS WAF web ACL rule
fixes.x: A university portal is being hardened against both abusive login traffic and large-scale denial-of-service events. Which statements about AWS WAF and AWS Shield are accurate? (Select TWO.)
fixes.e: AWS Shield absorbs volumetric attacks at the network and transport layers, while AWS WAF rate-based rules count requests per source and throttle any source exceeding a threshold. Shield Standard is applied automatically at no extra charge, with no subscription required and no dependency on a WAF web ACL, and WAF filters inbound web requests rather than outbound responses.

o: Federated access through a role that issues temporary sessions
An IAM user placed in a contractors group with a strict password policy
Long-term access keys attached to a tightly scoped permissions policy
A service control policy limiting which actions the contractor can take
fixes.x: A contractor needs console access for a two-week engagement, and the security team does not want any credentials lingering after the work ends. Which approach fits best?
fixes.e: Federated role access issues temporary credentials that stop working after the session duration, leaving nothing to clean up. An IAM user persists until someone deletes it no matter how strict its password policy, long-term access keys never expire on their own and grant programmatic rather than console access, and a service control policy only restricts permissions without granting sign-in or removing anything when the engagement ends.

o: A flat hourly rate applies to every function that is published
Cost is set by the memory reserved for the month, whether or not it is used
A minimum monthly invocation fee begins once the function goes live
Charges accrue only while function code is executing
fixes.x: A charity's donation page calls a small Lambda function to validate postal addresses, and traffic is sporadic and unpredictable. Which statement describes how the function is billed?
fixes.e: Lambda bills per request and for the milliseconds each invocation runs, so a function nobody calls costs nothing. Although the memory setting influences the per-millisecond price, memory is charged only during execution rather than reserved monthly, and there is no hourly rate or minimum fee for a published function.

o: The components no longer need to agree on a message format
End-to-end latency for each settlement message is reduced
Consumers no longer need error handling because the queue retries deliveries
A failure in the consumer does not immediately stop the producer
Each component can scale independently of the others
fixes.e: A queue buffers work so a slow or failing consumer does not halt the producer, and each side scales on its own schedule. The components must still agree on a message format, consumers still need error handling even though the queue redelivers unacknowledged messages, and inserting a queue adds an extra hop rather than reducing end-to-end latency.

o: Whether the Region offers the lowest prices for the services the system uses
Whether the Region keeps stored data within the required jurisdiction
Whether the Region carries the broadest set of compliance certifications and attestations
Whether the Region offers every managed service the records system plans to use
fixes.x: A hospital group in Germany must comply with a data-residency mandate covering patient records. When the group selects an AWS Region for its records system, which factor settles the decision?
fixes.e: Data residency is about physical location: data placed in a Region stays there unless the customer replicates it elsewhere, so choosing a Region inside Germany is what satisfies the mandate. A long list of compliance certifications attests to how AWS operates but does not change where the records physically live, and pricing or service breadth cannot override a residency requirement.

o: Per-team usage cannot be metered for internal chargeback in this model
Hypervisor overhead makes provisioning slower than on physical servers
Workloads from different teams cannot be isolated on shared hosts
Capacity is bounded by hardware the publisher already bought
fixes.x: A publisher runs an internal private cloud for its development teams. During seasonal production peaks, requests for new environments sit in a queue until other workloads wind down. Which limitation of the private cloud model does the wait illustrate?
fixes.e: A private cloud draws from a finite pool the publisher had to purchase up front, so requests queue whenever the installed hardware is fully committed and only clear when something is released. Hypervisor overhead would make provisioning uniformly slower rather than force requests to wait for other workloads to finish, and private clouds are fully capable of metering per-team usage and isolating workloads on shared hosts.

o: Capacity can be adjusted through APIs rather than purchase orders
Application code becomes the responsibility of AWS
Operating system patching is no longer required for any of its workloads
Monthly costs become a fixed amount that no longer varies with usage
The firm no longer maintains its own physical servers
fixes.x: A logistics firm now runs every application on AWS under an all-in cloud deployment. Which statements describe its current operating model? (Select TWO.)
fixes.e: An all-in cloud deployment removes ownership of physical servers and turns capacity changes into API calls instead of procurement cycles. Under the shared responsibility model, application code and OS patching on services like EC2 stay with the customer, and cloud spending is a variable expense that rises and falls with usage rather than a fixed monthly amount.

o: AWS pays list price for hardware and recovers the cost through service fees
A single campus orders a tiny fraction of the hardware volume AWS purchases
Volume discounts level off once an order reaches a few hundred servers
AWS's pricing advantage comes mainly from billing customers in advance
fixes.e: AWS aggregates purchasing across millions of customers, operating at a scale no single campus order can approach, and those economies of scale are what let it keep lowering prices. The claim that volume discounts level off after a few hundred servers would actually help the director's case if it were true, and AWS's advantage rests on purchasing scale, not on paying list price or collecting payment in advance.

o: Latency between the Region and the workload's end users
The number of edge locations AWS operates near the company's offices
Compliance and data-governance requirements
The default Region preselected in the AWS Management Console
The number of IAM roles already defined in the account
fixes.e: Region selection should weigh latency to the workload's end users and any compliance or data-governance obligations, alongside cost and service availability. Edge locations belong to the global content delivery network and serve users regardless of which Region hosts the workload, IAM is a global service whose roles work in every Region, and the console's preselected default is a convenience, not a selection criterion.

o: Data is encrypted only after it has been imported at the AWS data center
Customers must apply client-side encryption before copying data to the device
A dedicated AWS courier keeps custody of the device throughout shipment
Data is automatically encrypted and the device is tamper-resistant
fixes.e: Snowball encrypts data automatically with keys managed through AWS KMS and ships in a tamper-resistant enclosure with a Trusted Platform Module, so protection is in place before the device ever leaves the site. Client-side encryption is an optional extra rather than a requirement, and the device travels through standard carriers, not a dedicated AWS courier.

o: Serving cached game assets from AWS edge locations around the world
Replicating every workload to all Regions automatically by default
Applying Reserved Instance discounts from one Region in any other Region
Launching infrastructure in additional Regions without constructing facilities first
Transferring data between Regions at no cost over the AWS backbone
fixes.e: Because AWS already operates Regions across Europe and Asia, the studio can stand up infrastructure there without building anything, and edge locations cache game assets close to players to cut latency. Workloads are never replicated across Regions automatically, Reserved Instance discounts stay in the Region where they were purchased, and inter-Region data transfer is metered, not free.

o: Resource levels grow and shrink to track demand
Requests are rerouted to healthy servers when one stops responding
Complete environments can be stood up within minutes of a request
A predictable capacity baseline is committed up front at a lower rate
fixes.x: An application automatically launches extra servers while traffic is heavy and terminates them once it subsides. Which cloud characteristic does this demonstrate?
fixes.e: Elasticity is the characteristic where resource levels grow and shrink to track demand, usually through Auto Scaling. Rerouting requests around an unresponsive server describes high availability, standing up environments in minutes describes cloud agility, and committing a capacity baseline at a lower rate describes reserved pricing rather than demand-driven scaling.

o: A promotional credit automatically applied to the first monthly bill
An always-free allowance with no expiration date
A short-term trial that starts the first time a service is used
A 12-month free offer that begins when the account is created
fixes.x: A student opens a personal AWS account and wants to run a small Linux server for study without being charged for it. Which Free Tier category covers that usage?
fixes.e: The monthly allowance of small Linux instance hours belongs to the 12-month offers, which run from the day the account is created. Always-free allowances, such as a monthly quota of Lambda requests, never expire and form a separate category, while service trials are brief windows tied to first use of a specific service; the Free Tier is also not delivered as a promotional bill credit.

o: Charges are calculated from the highest usage level reached during the year
Charges follow what the workloads actually use as demand rises and falls
Charges are set by the amount of capacity provisioned at migration time
Charges apply only when usage exceeds the capacity originally planned
fixes.e: Consumption-based pricing bills for what is actually used, so the idle headroom that today sits at 88 percent stops generating cost instead of being paid for up front. Billing on provisioned capacity or on the year's high-water mark would preserve the over-provisioning penalty, and an overage-only scheme describes burst billing, not pay-as-you-go.

o: A step scaling policy
A simple scaling policy
A target tracking scaling policy
A scheduled scaling action
fixes.x: A web application team wants its EC2 Auto Scaling group to add and remove instances automatically so that average CPU utilization stays as close as possible to a value the team chooses. Which scaling approach does that?
fixes.e: Target tracking continuously adjusts group capacity to hold a chosen metric, such as average CPU utilization, near the specified value without the team defining alarms. Step scaling and simple scaling instead react to CloudWatch alarm breaches with adjustments the team must configure, and scheduled scaling changes capacity at preset times regardless of what the metric is doing.
